# Documentation

- Keep the main `README.md` concise and focused on an overview, getting started,
  and essential user-facing instructions.
- Do not append routine implementation details, debugging history, benchmark
  results, test inventories, or per-task change summaries to the README.
- Update existing README text when behavior changes; do not keep expanding it
  with a new section or bullet for every change.
- Put necessary technical detail in the most relevant existing documentation
  instead. Do not create documentation files merely to record completed work.
- Add substantial README content only when explicitly requested or essential
  for users to install, run, or use the application.
